hook.text: The US spends $4.3 trillion on healthcare. 75% goes to treating chronic diseases that prevention could reduce.

buildup.text: Preventive healthcare companies use wearables, genetic testing, and AI to catch diseases before symptoms appear.

discovery.text: Whoop and Oura ring track sleep, stress, and recovery. Data-driven prevention replaces symptom-based treatment.

twist.text: Insurance companies save money from prevention but rarely pay for it. The incentive system is backward.

climax.text: Preventive healthcare is cheaper and better—but the business model requires fixing misaligned incentives first.

punchline.text: 75% from preventable disease. Prevention is cheaper but nobody pays for it yet.

quiz.question: Why is preventive healthcare underinvested despite being cheaper?
options: Insurance incentives don't align with paying for prevention

details.summary: Preventive healthcare businesses shift the medical model from treating illness to preventing it through early screening, wearable monitoring, genetic risk assessment, and lifestyle intervention programs..
details.whyItMatters: Healthcare systems spend 90% of their budgets treating conditions that could have been prevented or caught earlier..
takeaways: Revenue comes from preventing disease rather than treating it
Wearables, screening, and lifestyle programs form the preventive toolkit
Employers and insurers fund preventive services to reduce future claims

faq.question: How do preventive healthcare businesses make money?
faq.answer: B2B contracts with employers paying for employee wellness programs. Subscription fees from consumers for monitoring and coaching services. Insurance company partnerships that share savings from prevented hospitalizations..

faq.question: What evidence shows preventive healthcare businesses deliver return on investment?
faq.answer: Livongo's diabetes prevention program reduced emergency visits by 20%. Employer wellness programs show $3-6 return per dollar invested through reduced absenteeism and claims. Early cancer detection programs dramatically reduce treatment costs. The ROI is strongest for chronic condition prevention.
